history.summary: IDENTITY/CORRECTION FLAG: There is NO Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy temple at Gudem Gutta. The hill temple (gutta) at Gudem village, Dandepalle mandal, Mancherial district, is the Gudem Gutta Shree Satyanarayana Swamy Temple - a Vishnu/Satyanarayana shrine established in 1964 when Govardhana Perumandla Swamy found swayambhu idols on the Ratnadri (Ratnapu Chevula) hill in a dream; the idols were anointed with Godavari water. Called 'Telangana's Annavaram' after the Andhra Satyanarayana shrine. One travel blog mislabels it as 'Gudem Gutta Sri Laxmi Narasimha Swamy Temple' - no other source supports a Narasimha shrine on this hill, so the CSV deity name appears to be an error. CSV TOWN FLAG: actual location is Gudem village, Dandepalle mandal, Mancherial district (not Ramagundam; about 50 km from Ramagundam, 32 km from Mancherial). Hilltop shrine on the banks of the Godavari with a steep climb; coordinates from geocoder FULL_ADDRESS match.

name: Gudem Gutta Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
town: Gudem (CSV town 'Ramagundam' is WRONG - the hill temple is at Gudem village, Dandepalle mandal, Mancherial district, about 50 km from Ramagundam)
town_description: Gudem is a village in Dandepalle mandal of Mancherial district on the banks of the Godavari. The Gudem Gutta hill (Ratnadri) rises above the village carrying the Satyanarayana Swamy temple with views over the river. About 32 km from Mancherial town, 34 km from Mancherial railway station, and about 50 km from Ramagundam; pilgrims flock here during Karthika Masam for a holy dip and Satyanarayana Vratam.
